skill.name: spec-driven-development
skill.description: Creates specs before coding. Use when starting a new project, feature, or significant change and no specification exists yet. Use when drafting a PRD or requirements document with objectives and scope, or when requirements are unclear, ambiguous, or only exist as a vague idea. Use when a single requirement spans several independently testable capabilities and needs decomposing into a capability map of modules before specifying.
skill.summary: Guides teams from clarified requirements to reviewed specifications, plans, tasks, and implementation.
skill.author: addyosmani

content.user_title: Plan Software Work With Clear Specifications
content.value_statement: Unclear requirements cause rework, missed assumptions, and poorly ordered implementation tasks. This skill guides teams through reviewed specifications, dependency-aware plans, and verifiable tasks before coding.
actual_capabilities: Clarifies ambiguous project or feature requirements before implementation.
Creates capability maps for requests with independently testable modules.
Structures specifications with objectives, commands, project structure, style, testing, and boundaries.
Reframes vague requests into specific and testable success criteria.
Breaks approved plans into dependency-ordered tasks with acceptance and verification criteria.
Defines review gates between specification, planning, tasks, and implementation.
limitations: It does not implement code, run tests, or verify technical claims by itself.
It depends on accurate project context and human answers to clarification questions.
It does not replace architecture review, security review, or product decision-making.
Referenced companion skills and external specification tools must exist in the working environment.

use_cases.title: Shape a New Product Feature
use_cases.description: Turn an initial feature idea into an approved specification with user goals, boundaries, success criteria, and an implementation plan.

use_cases.title: Decompose a Multi-Module Initiative
use_cases.description: Map independently testable capabilities, record dependency direction, and create module-specific specifications in build order.

use_cases.title: Make Requirements Testable
use_cases.description: Convert vague outcomes into measurable acceptance criteria, verification steps, and focused implementation tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise specification for this feature: [feature]. Ask clarifying questions first, then define the objective, users, scope, success criteria, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify an Ambiguous Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this request: [request]. List the assumptions you would need to confirm, ask focused questions, and reframe the final requirements as testable success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Module Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Decompose this initiative into independently testable modules: [initiative]. Create a capability map with stable identifiers, dependencies, build order, and a specification outline for each module.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Implementation Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this approved specification and plan: [documents], create dependency-ordered tasks. Give each task acceptance criteria, a verification step, and the files or areas likely to change.

output_examples.output: Success criteria: largest contentful paint under 2.5 seconds on a 4G connection; initial data load under 500 milliseconds; cumulative layout shift under 0.1.

output_examples.input: Build account, billing, notifications, and reporting capabilities.
output: Capability map: identity owns accounts and sessions; billing depends on identity; notifications depends on identity; reporting depends on billing and notifications.
Build order: identity, then billing and notifications, then reporting.

best_practices: Confirm assumptions before drafting specification content.
Use stable module identifiers and explicit dependency direction.
Require human approval at each phase before advancing.
anti_patterns: Starting implementation before requirements and success criteria are approved.
Hiding ambiguous decisions inside a specification without asking.
Creating tasks without acceptance criteria or a verification step.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for new projects, significant features, ambiguous requirements, or changes that span multiple modules.

faq.question: When should I skip it?
faq.answer: Skip it for single-line fixes, typo corrections, and small changes with clear requirements.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. It prepares specifications, plans, tasks, and review gates before implementation.

faq.question: What does the specification include?
faq.answer: It covers the objective, commands, project structure, code style, testing strategy, boundaries, success criteria, and open questions.

faq.question: How does it handle large initiatives?
faq.answer: It creates a capability map, records dependencies, sets a build order, and creates a specification for each module.

faq.question: Does it replace technical review?
faq.answer: No. Human reviewers still approve assumptions, scope, architecture, security concerns, and readiness for implementation.
